question: Require data centers to pay additional fees to offset their electricity demand
note: Registered-voter subset of 804 VA adults, fielded Jun 22-Jul 6 2026. Oppose share not reported. Same poll: 72% of RVs oppose the data center sales tax exemption.

question: Continue the sales-tax exemption for data centers vs. end the incentives
note: Reverse-worded: sup = % who want to end data center tax incentives (67%), opp = % supporting continuing the exemption (26%). Registered voters, Mar 26-31 2026; Washington Post story reprinted by Anchorage Daily News.

question: Mandatory fair share: require AI companies/data centers to pay the full cost of the power they use
note: Partisan/advocacy (CAP). Spring 2026; memo gives no sample size or oppose shares. Voluntary fair-share version: 56%.

question: Ban utility 'junk fees' (charging customers for lobbying, PR, trade association dues)
note: Partisan/advocacy (CAP). Spring 2026; no sample size or oppose shares. Ban on fuel surcharges: 61%.

question: Federally funded freeze on electricity rates
note: Partisan/advocacy (CAP). Federal (not state) rate freeze; spring 2026; no sample size or oppose shares.

question: Bar shifting data center energy costs onto consumers' utility bills
note: Advocacy-sponsored (coalition backing the POWER Act); likely voters, Mar 16-19 2026; agree share only (84% strongly). Overall POWER Act regulation: 68% support, 21% oppose.

question: Require data centers to supply their own energy rather than draw from the public grid
note: PA adults, Nov 19-23 2025; 24% neutral. Proxy for making data centers bear their own power costs (own generation, not cost allocation).

question: Importance of a safeguard requiring data centers to pay for grid upgrades, new generation and their full electricity costs so other customers see no rate hikes
note: Importance scale, not support/oppose: sup = very+somewhat important (74.2% very), opp = not very/not at all important. Likely voters, Apr 28-May 1 2026. Same poll: no extra tax incentives/NDAs for data centers 85.5% important, 11.5% not.

question: Require data centers to pay the full cost of the energy and grid infrastructure they need
note: Advocacy-sponsored (climate coalition). RVs nationwide, Apr 9-19 2026; support only reported. Requiring data centers to fund transmission/grid upgrades: 71%.

question: Suspend the federal gas tax to reduce gas prices
note: RVs, May 11-12 2026, online. After being told the tax raises ~$36B/yr: 58% favor, 28% oppose.

question: Temporarily suspend the Massachusetts state gas tax
note: MA residents, Jun 15-21 2022; oppose share not given in release. Older poll; a 69% 'UMass poll' figure cited by Rep. Smola in Oct 2026 (NBC Boston) could not be traced to a release, so not used.

question: Make data centers pay more for their electricity
note: NJ RVs/likely voters, Oct 9-15 2025; oppose share not reported in release (D 77, I 73, R 56).

question: Tighter regulation of power producers and distributors to bring down energy costs
note: Loose proxy for utility accountability (general tighter regulation, not specifically fee caps or lobbying limits). Oppose not reported. Same poll as the FDU data-center item.

pollster: University of Houston Hobby School of Public Affairs
question: Require data center companies to pay for the grid upgrades needed to serve their facilities
note: Likely voters, Oct 10-14 2026. Report EXCLUDES 'unsure' responses, so shares are of those with an opinion (cannot re-derive all-respondent shares); likely overstates support vs. other polls.

pollster: SurveyUSA / Ohio Northern University Institute for Civics and Public Policy
question: Tax breaks for data centers (support vs. oppose)
note: Reverse-worded: sup = % opposing data center tax breaks, opp = % supporting them. Ohio adults; field dates not stated (article published Oct 22 2026).

question: Subsidies for local data centers (support vs. oppose)
note: Reverse-worded: sup = % opposing local data center subsidies, opp = % supporting; 12% unsure. Field dates not stated (article published Jul 23 2026); toplines at https://kstp.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/PollData.pdf (not opened).
